belief: “Other people can see that I am different now, and they will keep their distance.”
belief_plain: Other people can see that I am different now, and they will keep their distance
origins: Being hurt can change how you carry yourself. You may feel marked, odd, or easy to spot. Sometimes people really have been clumsy or distant. The lie says they can see that you are different and therefore they will keep away, as if your wound were a sign on your face. Most people cannot read your history. Some who know it can stay. You do not have to explain what happened in order to test this. A counselor can help you sort fear from fact. A counselor can help you work with this at a pace that is safe. You do not have to do it alone, or all at once.
self: If they knew, they would step back.
I should stay away so I do not make people uncomfortable.
I am too different to belong.
Looking fine is the only way to be tolerated.
God is probably keeping His distance too.
replacement: Some people may notice I am struggling, and that does not mean everyone will keep their distance. God is near, and safe people can stay.
